quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you not to make a U-turn. Do not turn around at this location.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can cross it to pass. Drivers in both directions must stay in their own lane.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less serious with beer than with wine.
Is less serious with wine than with beer.
Is most serious with hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment the same way. The type does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: How can you avoid the dangers of drinking and driving?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.explanation: The best way is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol makes it harder to make safe choices, so decide before you start drinking.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Slowing down reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
If it means driving off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right when a vehicle is turning left and a passing lane is available. You can also pass on the right on roads with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or being careless.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely dangerous.
Not a concern.
Just as safe as other driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Focus on driving to prevent crashes.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.
No, never.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in a vehicle on a public road. You cannot have an open alcohol container in any area of the vehicle normally used by the driver or passengers.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot. Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line of vehicles at a stop sign. The vehicles ahead pass through and there is no traffic coming. What should you do?

options.text: You may go through the intersection without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign before going forward.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign before going forward.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before going forward. Do not skip the stop just because other cars are moving.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your physical condition does not make you drive unsafely?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how any medicine affects your driving.
Only drive within your physical abilities.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. Be aware of your limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should a driver do if involved in an accident?

options.text: Stop at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If you are in an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Stay out of traffic lanes to avoid being hit. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the correct lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane there.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Bicycle store.
Soft shoulders.

questions.explanation: This sign shows a bicycle crossing or path. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles may cross or ride next to traffic here.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: Your tires work less well as you drive faster.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
The road becomes more slippery as you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires work less well as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less grip your tires have. If you go too fast, your tires can lose contact with the road and you will slide on water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: Why should drivers use extra care around snowplows?

options.text: Blowing snow can lower your ability to see.
They are wider than other vehicles.
They move slower than other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drive carefully around snowplows because they are wider and slower than other vehicles. Snowplows create clouds of snow that lower visibility in the area.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest.
Move your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired yet.
